editorial:
Imagine being stuck in a small room for the whole movie, just listening to a phone call. That is exactly how this story starts. You follow a cop who got demoted to the 911 dispatch desk because of some mistakes in his past. He is just trying to get through his shift when he gets a call from a terrified woman who says she has been kidnapped. Since he cannot leave his desk, he has to use his voice and his brain to save her. It feels like a race against time, and the tension builds up quickly as you try to piece together what is actually happening based only on what you hear over the phone.

Jake Gyllenhaal does an amazing job here because he is the only person on screen, but he keeps you totally hooked. The way the story flips your expectations is the best part. While it might feel slow at first because there is no big action, the twists make it feel like a rollercoaster. If you like mysteries that make you think, you will love this. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best quality, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. It is a tight, smart ride that proves you do not need a huge budget to tell a great story.
endingExplained: You find out that the woman on the phone was not actually kidnapped. She was the one who kidnapped another woman and was calling 911 to make herself look like a victim. She was playing a game with the officer to mess with his head. In the end, the police find the real victim and arrest the caller. The officer realizes he was tricked, but he still manages to save the innocent person.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological puzzles and great acting.
